Village Intel
Turn the 'ask about the area' dialogue on or off.
Town notables too
Off: only village notables (headmen and rural notables) can be asked. On: town notables (merchants, artisans, gang leaders) can be asked as well.
Search radius
How far from the village (in campaign map units) a notable can have heard of parties and hideouts. Roughly 5 units is an hour's ride.
Most sightings per answer
The most parties or hideouts a notable will describe in one answer, nearest first.
Hours before asking again
Within this many hours, asking the same notable the same question repeats their earlier answer for free instead of giving a new one.
Truthful hideout reports mark the map
When a notable tells the truth about a hideout, it is marked on the campaign map. Handy, but it also tells you when a notable lied.
Chance to know: on the doorstep
Chance a notable has heard of a party right next to the village. It falls off evenly to the far value at the edge of the search radius.
Chance to know: edge of radius
Chance a notable has heard of a party at the edge of the search radius.
Bonus for hideouts
Hideouts don't move, so locals are more likely to know where they are.
Bonus for armies
Armies are hard to miss.
Base chance to lie
Chance to lie about a sighting when the notable likes you exactly as much as they like the party in question.
Lie chance per relation point
Trust = (notable's relation with you) - (notable's relation with the party). Each point of trust lowers the lie chance by this much, and each point of distrust raises it.
Maximum chance to lie
No notable lies more often than this, however much they dislike you or like the party in question.
Dishonesty per Honor level
Each level of negative Honor adds this to the notable's lie chance; each positive level takes half of it away.
Loyalty to own realm
Added to a notable's relation with a party that belongs to the village's own realm (they protect their own lords).
Hatred of the village's enemies
Subtracted from a notable's relation with a party whose realm is at war with the village's realm.
Relation with bandits
A notable's relation with bandits before Honor is applied. Villagers usually hate them.
Bandit sympathy per Honor level
Each level of negative Honor makes the notable this much friendlier with bandits (they may be in league with them); each positive level makes them this much more hostile.
Skill lead to notice a lie
You notice a lie when your Charm, Scouting or Roguery is higher than the notable's by more than this. 0 means any higher skill is enough.
Pressing: base chance
Chance that calling out a lie makes the notable tell the truth, before your skill lead and relation are added.
Pressing: chance per skill or relation point
Each point by which your best skill (Charm, Scouting or Roguery) beats the notable's, and each point of relation, adds this to the pressing chance. Bad relation takes it away.
Pressing: relation lost on failure
How much relation you lose when you call a notable a liar and they won't back down.
Relation to talk at all
Notables whose relation with you is at or below this refuse to tell you anything.
Relation for free information
Notables whose relation with you is at or above this tell you for free.
Price: enemy parties
Base asking price in denars for news of enemy war parties, at 0 relation.
Price: bandit gangs
Base asking price in denars for news of roaming bandit gangs, at 0 relation.
Price: bandit hideouts
Base asking price in denars for the whereabouts of bandit hideouts, at 0 relation.
Extra price per bad relation point
Each point of relation below 0 raises the price by this fraction. Each point above 0 lowers it by half as much.
Charm discount at 300
Discount you get with 300 Charm. Scales linearly with your Charm skill.
Chance goods are accepted
Chance the notable will take food or trade goods from your inventory as payment, if you have enough.
Chance only goods will do
When goods are accepted, the chance the notable refuses coin and wants the goods instead.
Goods markup
How much base value of goods the notable wants for each denar of the price.
Relation gained when paying
Relation you gain with a notable each time you pay them in gold or goods.
Allow persuasion

When a notable asks to be paid, you can instead try to talk them round with the game's normal persuasion system (one try per question). Success gets the answer for free and gives skill experience like other persuasions.
